solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heckle leader caught in booze store where people have reservations

indicators.note: something caught in a place is held inside it, so the letter for caught sits within the shop

parts.note: to boo is to jeer at a speaker
a king is a ruler or leader
British slang for an off-licence, a shop selling alcohol to take away
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A heckler's ringleader is nabbed inside an off-licence, oddly placed beside where people book.
explanation.walkthrough: An offie is British slang for an off-licence, a shop selling drink to take away; C goes inside it before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A booking office is the counter at a station or theatre where tickets and seats are reserved in advance.

clue.text: Lively people's party cancelled with father around

definitions.note: the clue's 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance party

indicators.note: around says the word for father wraps itself about the word for cancelled

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a male parent
an event that is off has been called off

explanation.surface: Energetic partygoers learn their do has been called off, with Dad hovering about.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball of fire is an idiom for a person full of energy and enthusiasm, so the plural covers several of them.

clue.text: Work in the theatre, or just over half of one

indicators.note: only slightly more than half of the following word survives, so the tail is cut away

parts.note: one refers back to a work in the theatre: surgery done in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: A question of whether a stage production counts as work, or only partly so.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is read twice: a stage for the definition and an operating theatre for the wordplay, whose nine-letter word keeps its first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic musical composition staged in an opera house or playhouse.

clue.text: Appeal during boring game creates irritation

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: boring here means drilling into, so the short word bores its way inside the game

parts.note: chess is a board game
in means during, as in in the night

explanation.surface: Being made to play a tedious game of chess is enough to make anyone irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like an adjective describing the game, but it means drilling into it; IT for sex appeal is old slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchiness is a tickling skin sensation, and irritation is the general word for that kind of discomfort.

clue.text: Fellow about ready to fight big girl's blouse, say

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for fellow goes around the other part

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a fellow
to arm is to equip and make ready for battle

explanation.surface: A man squares up for a fight with a wimp, called a big girl's blouse in British slang.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a big girl's blouse is a feeble, cowardly man; read literally it is just an item of clothing, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A blouse of any size is an item of clothing, so it serves as an example of a piece of apparel.

clue.text: Maiden king's taken in hand

indicators.note: taken in means held within, so the king's letter is gripped by the hand

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A young woman's hand is held by a king, as in a courtly betrothal.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden as an adjective means initial or inaugural, as in a maiden voyage or a maiden speech.

clue.text: Lover got a Roman imperator somewhat upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way
somewhat means only a part of the phrase that follows is used

parts.note: the run of letters spans got, a, Roman and the start of imperator

explanation.surface: A lover received an emperor's anger from a Roman ruler, who was rather put out.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorato is a male lover or sweetheart, from Italian for one who is enamoured.

clue.text: … stripped off woman often painted naked

parts.note: surface reading: someone has undressed, continuing the previous clue
setter's reading: the first woman of Genesis, shown unclothed in countless paintings

explanation.surface: Following on from the lover, a woman has undressed to model for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first woman lived unclothed in Eden, and artists from Dürer onwards have painted her nude.

clue.text: Picked up medium for sculptor or modern artist

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a broadcast

parts.note: clay is the material a sculptor models with

explanation.surface: Someone collects the right material for a sculptor or for a contemporary painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Klee was a Swiss-German painter of the twentieth century, a leading figure in modernism.

clue.text: Device for paying person with a transport phobia?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the machine you insert or tap a bank card on
second meaning, whimsical: one who dreads cars

explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, the phrase becomes car dreader, a person afraid of motor vehicles; the question mark flags the invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: A card reader is the payment terminal that reads a debit or credit card at a till.

clue.text: At home in America's capital, say

indicators.note: a capital is a word's initial letter, so only the head of America is used

parts.note: the opening letter of America

indicators.note: in places the word for home inside the following letters

parts.note: to state is to say
at home is in, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Someone is at home in Washington, the capital of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home' reads as one phrase, but At alone is the definition: the chemical symbol of the element.
explanation.definitionFit: At is the periodic table symbol for astatine, a rare radioactive halogen element.

clue.text: Skill about carrying common person in carriage

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the word for skill holds the common person inside
about means turned round, so the word for skill is read backwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation
oik is British slang for a coarse, uncouth person

explanation.surface: A skilled coachman gives a lift to a commoner in his carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Oik is British slang for an ill-mannered, common person.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian carriage or sleigh drawn by three horses abreast.

clue.text: Big profit this person's invested in case of trouble, being a waiter?

parts.note: to make a killing is to win a big profit

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, like money placed in a fund
a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters of trouble are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of trouble
this person is the speaker, I, and the apostrophe s makes I'm

explanation.surface: An investor makes a fortune and stashes it away as insurance against hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: A waiter here is not a server in a restaurant but someone waiting; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing time means passing idle hours while waiting for something, which is what someone who waits does.

clue.text: Mercian king returning by wild desert covered in greenery

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the king's name is read from the end

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of central England

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of the next word run riot

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An old English king comes back past a desert that has turned green.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was a kingdom of Anglo-Saxon England, and Offa, builder of Offa's Dyke, its best-known king.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that has been afforested has been planted with trees, so it is now wooded and green.

clue.text: Attendants in group of monks can't be trusted

parts.note: a religious order is a community of monks
someone who lies cannot be trusted

explanation.surface: Servants at a monastery turn out to be untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderlies are hospital or military assistants who carry out routine tasks and wait on others.

clue.text: Producer of 2 into diet changes, eating unknown quantity

definitions.note: 2 is the answer to 2-down, an opera

indicators.note: changes means altering the arrangement of the preceding words
eating means swallowing something, so the rearranged letters take in another

parts.note: the letters of into diet, rearranged
in algebra x, y and z are the unknowns

explanation.surface: A composer of operas goes on a diet with an unpredictable amount of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaetano Donizetti was an Italian composer of many operas, including Lucia di Lammermoor.

clue.text: Very large drilling article close to mine shaft

indicators.note: drilling means boring into, so the size letters go inside

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
XL is the clothing size extra large

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter of mine is used

parts.note: the final letter of mine

explanation.surface: A huge machine is boring through near a mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine shaft' reads as one phrase, but shaft alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod or spindle on which a wheel turns, a kind of rotating bar.

clue.text: Split ends occasionally spotted, perhaps

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Damaged hair tips are noticed from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Pied means patchy in two or more colours, like a magpie; being spotted is one such pattern.

clue.text: Almost performed The Merchant of Venice in US city

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word for performed loses its last letter

parts.note: to sing is to perform a song
Antonio is the title character, the merchant, in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: An acting company nearly finished staging a Shakespeare comedy while touring America.
explanation.walkthrough: The play's title role is not Shylock but Antonio, the merchant who borrows the money.
explanation.definitionFit: San Antonio is a large city in Texas, home of the Alamo.

clue.text: Part of an atom of gas probed by London university

indicators.note: something probed by another has that thing pushed inside it

parts.note: neon is a noble gas
UCL is University College London

explanation.surface: London academics investigate the atomic structure of a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleon is a proton or neutron, the particles that make up the nucleus of an atom.

clue.text: One game to plug venture capital

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so these letters are stuffed inside the word for venture

parts.note: to venture money is to bet it
I is the Roman numeral one
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A sporting event is used to promote a venture capital fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venture capital' reads as one finance term, but capital alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Here capital means a seat of national government, and this Mediterranean city is where Lebanon is governed from.

clue.text: Best rating for literary motif

parts.note: top means the best
a rating is a sailor below officer rank, such as an OS, ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A reviewer awards a book's recurring theme a five-star score.
explanation.walkthrough: In the navy a rating is an enlisted sailor, and OS stands for ordinary seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A topos is a conventional theme or commonplace that recurs throughout literature.

clue.text: Old fraud in business, having time for Buddhism?

parts.note: Co. is short for company
a Zen age would be an era given over to that school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: Swindling in a company that has made time for meditation.
explanation.walkthrough: Zen is a school of Buddhism and an age is a time, so a Zen age is a playful time for Buddhism.
explanation.definitionFit: Cozenage is an archaic word for cheating or deception, from to cozen, meaning to trick.

clue.text: Shower heralds ultimately clean feet, with area scrubbed

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of clean is used

parts.note: the last letter of clean

indicators.note: scrubbed means cancelled, so the letter for area is wiped out

parts.note: iambi are metrical feet of one short and one long syllable
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Bathing instructions: wash your feet but leave out one part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: An iamb is a poetic foot, and its plural can be iambi.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi are dark rain clouds, which arrive ahead of a downpour and so announce it.

clue.text: Manuscript proceeds haltingly, and is translated into French after a year

parts.note: p.a. is per annum, Latin for a year
someone who limps moves along unevenly
est is the French for is

explanation.surface: A document's progress stalls before it is rendered into French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a year' puts the per annum letters first.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a parchment manuscript scraped clean and reused, with traces of earlier writing visible.

clue.text: Cliff, no good, going around bend

indicators.note: going around means turning about, so the letters run back to front
no good means without G, the abbreviation for good

parts.note: a crag is a steep rock face

explanation.surface: A man named Cliff, no use at driving, takes a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff looks like a man's name, but here it is a rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a curved line or part of a circle, the shape of a curve.

clue.text: Primarily, milady's helper?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so just the opening letter of milady's is taken

parts.note: the first letter of milady's
an aid is a helper or assistant

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the wordplay builds the word and the full phrase describes it, the question mark admitting the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady's maid is a servant whose chief job is attending to her mistress.

clue.text: Something traveller has seen with visit abroad, observing capitals?

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a fresh order

parts.note: a traveller carries a suitcase
the letters of seen and visit, rearranged

explanation.surface: A tourist sees the sights of foreign capital cities.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitals here are capital letters, not cities; the question mark flags the shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that is case-sensitive treats upper and lower case letters as different, so it pays attention to them.
